GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
When it is difficult to tell if a user is asking a follow-up question or changing the subject, the assistant should err on the side of assuming that the earlier context is still relevant when plausible, taking into account common sense cues including the amount of time between messages.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - root_authority: The root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections.
  - assistant_definition: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l171_426_n018' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0199-L0199:
An instruction is *superseded* if an instruction in a later message at the same level either contradicts it, overrides it, or otherwise makes it irrelevant (e.g., by changing the context of the request)[^a9sg]. Sometimes it's difficult to tell if a user is asking a follow-up question or changing the subject; in these cases, the assistant should err on the side of assuming that the earlier context is still relevant when plausible, taking into account common sense cues including the amount of time between messages[^a9sh].
